headline_marked: Child and woman die as [[boat carrying Rohingya refugees sinks]] off Teknaf
headline: Child and woman die as boat carrying Rohingya refugees sinks off Teknaf
summary: Two bodies were recovered and one person remains missing after a boat collided with an object near the shore in Cox's Bazar.
details: A boat carrying Rohingya refugees and two Bangladeshi nationals sank early Tuesday morning off the Teknaf coast in Cox’s Bazar.
Coast Guard personnel rescued 16 people, who were handed over to the Teknaf Model Police Station for verification.
Police recovered the bodies of a three-year-old child and a 25-year-old woman from the sea, while another woman remains missing.
The incident occurred around 1:00 AM at the Karachi Para sea beach in Baharchhara union.
According to survivors, the boat apparently collided with something near the shore before sinking.
Two of the survivors, including a Buddhist man from Ukhia, stated they were returning to Bangladesh after serving prison terms in Myanmar.
The rescued Rohingyas were identified as residents of various camps in Bangladesh who had traveled to Myanmar and were returning.
The bodies of the deceased have been sent to Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital for autopsy.
Teknaf Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Saiful Islam confirmed the incident and stated that rescued individuals will be questioned before legal action is taken.
caption:
A 3-year-old child and a woman died after their boat sank off the Teknaf coast.

A boat carrying Rohingya refugees and two Bangladeshi nationals sank early Tuesday morning off the Teknaf coast in Cox’s Bazar.

Coast Guard personnel rescued 16 people, who were handed over to the Teknaf Model Police Station for verification.

Police recovered the bodies of a three-year-old child and a 25-year-old woman from the sea, while another woman remains missing.

The incident occurred around 1:00 AM at the Karachi Para sea beach in Baharchhara union.

According to survivors, the boat apparently collided with something near the shore before sinking.

Two of the survivors, including a Buddhist man from Ukhia, stated they were returning to Bangladesh after serving prison terms in Myanmar.

The rescued Rohingyas were identified as residents of various camps in Bangladesh who had traveled to Myanmar and were returning.

The bodies of the deceased have been sent to Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital for autopsy.

Teknaf Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Saiful Islam confirmed the incident and stated that rescued individuals will be questioned before legal action is taken.

topic: deep depression forms in bay of bengal
headline_marked: Bay of Bengal: [[Deep depression forms]], ports on alert
headline: Bay of Bengal: Deep depression forms, ports on alert
summary: A low-pressure system has intensified into a deep depression, prompting warning signal No. 3 at major sea ports including Chattogram and Cox's Bazar.
details: A low-pressure system over the Bay of Bengal has intensified into a deep depression, moving northwest toward the Indian coast.
At 9pm Tuesday, the system was centered over the west-central and adjoining northwest Bay, approximately 695km to 875km southwest of major Bangladeshi ports.
Meteorologist Khandaker Hafizur Rahman stated that while it is unlikely to develop into a cyclone for now, it may bring rain to the southern and southwestern parts of the country.
Winds near the center are reaching 50kmph, rising to 60kmph in gusts, which may affect sea ports and coastal areas.
As a result, Chattogram, Cox’s Bazar, Mongla, and Payra ports have been instructed to keep local warning signal No. 3 hoisted.
Fishing boats and trawlers in the north Bay have been advised to remain close to the coast and operate cautiously until further notice.
caption:
A deep depression has formed in the Bay of Bengal, putting major sea ports on high alert.

A low-pressure system over the Bay of Bengal has intensified into a deep depression, moving northwest toward the Indian coast.

At 9pm Tuesday, the system was centered over the west-central and adjoining northwest Bay, approximately 695km to 875km southwest of major Bangladeshi ports.

Meteorologist Khandaker Hafizur Rahman stated that while it is unlikely to develop into a cyclone for now, it may bring rain to the southern and southwestern parts of the country.

Winds near the center are reaching 50kmph, rising to 60kmph in gusts, which may affect sea ports and coastal areas.

As a result, Chattogram, Cox’s Bazar, Mongla, and Payra ports have been instructed to keep local warning signal No. 3 hoisted.

Fishing boats and trawlers in the north Bay have been advised to remain close to the coast and operate cautiously until further notice.
